name: Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH
summary: Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner is a 650-staff, EUR 151 M seal maker owned by Ravensteiner Holding AG, financially stable (credit index 159, unchanged). It is running at very high utilisation: it allocates standard mechanical seals based on last year's call-offs, cannot confirm our full forecast for single-sourced part:340010, quotes longer lead times and serves customers with firm long-term commitments first. We are only 0.5 % of its turnover, so it does not need us, while we depend on it for part:340010.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager up to 2 % price change; above that the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks (group: Ravensteiner Holding AG)

negotiation_pattern: Asks moderate annual increases of 1.1-7.0 % (mean 3.18 %) and settles far lower (mean 1.01 %, settled minus asked -2.17 pp). In the last round (Nov/Dec 2025) it accepted 0 % on all three parts, and 0 % was also the outcome in 5 of 9 renewals overall. It does not fight hard on price. Its leverage now is capacity: it links extra or confirmed volume to a binding 12-month commitment rather than to price.
wants: binding long-term commitment (12+ months) and firm forecasts to plan scarce capacity
reliable on-time payment (we pay late 76 % of the time)
a modest price increase for 2027, kept under the 2 % committee threshold
protects: capacity allocation and delivery confirmations (allocates by last year's call-offs)
lead_time_days (currently longer than the agreed 42 days)
unit_price reductions (no reason to cut while sold out; anything above 2 % goes to the pricing committee)

trades.give: contract_months up: binding 12-month volume commitment / extend framework beyond 2027-06-30
trades.get: confirmed full forecast allocation for part:340010 and lead_time_days back to the contractual 42 days
trades.why: It explicitly prioritises customers with firm long-term commitments.

trades.give: volume_per_year: firm rolling 12-month forecast with frozen near-term call-offs
trades.get: unit_price held flat for 2027 (0 %, as in the last renewal)
trades.why: Planning security is worth more to a full plant than a small price increase; past settlements were 0 %.

trades.give: payment discipline: pay strictly on day 30 (no late payments)
trades.get: no price increase, or any increase capped below 2 %
trades.why: Cheap for us; removes a reason for them to rank us low in allocation.

trades.give: effective_date: accept a small increase only if forced, effective no earlier than 2027-04-01
trades.get: capacity reservation for part:340010 in the commitment
trades.why: Staying under the 2 % approval line avoids slow committee loops and secures supply first.

arguments.point: Allocation follows last year's call-offs. Our spend grew from EUR 700k (FY2024) to EUR 816k (FY2026), so our allocation share should cover the full forecast.
The framework agreement runs to 2027-06-30 with auto-extension, and the 42-day lead time is contractual. Longer lead times break the agreement.
Prices are fixed per calendar year, and changes require written notice at least 90 days before year-end (about 2026-10-02). No notice is on file, so 2027 prices should stay unchanged.
OTD of 79.5 % is well below the 95 % contractual target. Acknowledge the ppm improvement (412 to 270), but ask for a delivery recovery plan.
Part:340011 has a second source (sup:70440, 60 % quota). We can shift volume there, which frees Ravensteiner capacity for part:340010.

avoid: Price-down demands based on should-cost: the +23 % gap on part:340010 rests on an estimate with only 5 % confidence, and a sold-out supplier will not cut.
Threatening to resource part:340010: there is no alternative source, and we are only 0.5 % of its turnover.
Requests needing over 2 % movement: they trigger the pricing committee and delays.
Asking for extra volume without offering a binding commitment.
tone: Professional and partnership-oriented. Lead with commitment and planning security, firm on the contract terms, no threats.
red_flags: Supply risk on single-sourced part:340010: full forecast not confirmed, lead times above the agreed 42 days.
OTD trending down (81.8 to 79.5 %) against the 95 % target; 1 open 8D, last complaint 2026-09-02.
We pay late 76 % of the time (avg 1.9 days), which could lower our priority in allocation.
The supplier can terminate with 90 days' notice ahead of the 2027-06-30 end; we have low leverage at 0.5 % of its turnover.

evidence.claim: Very high utilisation; full forecast for part:340010 cannot be confirmed; lead times longer; firm long-term commitments get priority
Standard mechanical seals allocated in line with last year's call-offs
Strong order intake; additional volume only against a binding 12-month commitment
Price changes above 2 % need pricing committee approval (meets every two weeks)
Last renewal settled at 0 % on all three parts despite asks of 1.1-2.5 %
Prices fixed per calendar year; 90-day notice before year-end required for changes
OTD 79.5 % vs 95 % target; ppm improved to 270; scorecard green, class A
Part:340010 price 29.89 vs should-cost 24.31 (+23 %), estimate confidence only 5 %
Group-owned, financially stable (credit index 159 unchanged, equity ratio 28.8 %)

indicators.credit_index: 159 (12 months ago 159; higher is worse, >300 weak)
price_vs_should_cost_no_margin: part:340010: price 29.89 vs cost:340010 24.31 (its own plant): +23.0 %
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 81.8, ppm 412) → 2026Q1 green (otd 81.6, ppm 405) → 2026Q2 green (otd 79.7, ppm 366) → 2026Q3 green (otd 79.5, ppm 270)
